t.2.39.1: To Kausalyā, that most excellent of women, who was lamenting in this way, Sumitrā, who stood firm in dharma, spoke these words in accordance with dharma.
t.2.39.2: O noble lady, that son of yours is the best of men, endowed with true virtues. What use to you is this lamenting, or this piteous weeping?
t.2.39.4: Rāma, the most excellent, abides in dharma, which is rightly and ever practised by the virtuous and whose fruit arises after death; he is never to be grieved for.
t.2.39.3: O noble lady, your mighty son, who has gone away abandoning the kingdom, has done right by his great-souled father, a speaker of truth among truth-speakers.
t.2.39.6: Though accustomed to comfort, and knowing full well what sorrow lies in dwelling in the forest, Vaidehī follows your righteous-souled son.
t.2.39.5: And Lakṣmaṇa, ever sinless and compassionate toward all beings, conducts himself toward him with the highest devotion; this is a gain for that great-souled one.
t.2.39.7: Your son, the mighty lord who waves throughout the world the banner that is his fame, and who is devoted to self-restraint, truth and his vows, what is there that he has not attained?
t.2.39.8: Having recognized the manifest purity and supreme greatness of Rāma, the sun will not scorch his body with its rays.
t.2.39.9: At all times the auspicious, pleasant wind, issuing forth from the forests and tempered in its coolness and warmth, will attend upon Rāghava.
t.2.39.10: As he lies asleep at night, the sinless one, the moon, embracing him like a father and caressing him with its cool rays, will gladden him.
t.2.39.11: He, the one of great might, to whom Brahmā gave divine weapons after seeing the lord of the Dānavas, the son of Timidhvaja, slain in battle.
t.2.39.12: Together with the Earth, with Vaidehī, and with Śrī, Rāma, that bull among men, will soon be consecrated, together with these three.
t.2.39.14: Seeing your son, together with his friends, saluting you, you will soon shed tears of joy, like a bank of clouds in the rainy season.
t.2.39.13: He whom you watched departing while your eyes shed tears born of grief: soon you will pour from your eyes tears born of joy.
t.2.39.15: Your son, the granter of boons, having swiftly returned to Ayodhyā, will press your feet with his two soft and sturdy hands.
t.2.39.16: Hearing those words of Lakṣmaṇa's mother, the grief in the body of Rāma's mother, the wife of the king, vanished at once, like an autumn cloud that holds little water.
